Based on the provided file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a system design diagram for this documentation website project. This is a documentation site built with Docusaurus, which is a modern static site generator.

Here's how to structure the system design diagram:

   - Node.js Runtime Environment
   - NPM Package Manager
   - Local Development Server

b. Build System Layer:
   - Docusaurus Build System
   - Babel Transpiler (noted from babel.config.mjs)
   - PostCSS/Tailwind Processing (from postcss.config.js and tailwind.config.ts)

c. Content Structure Layer:
   - Documentation Content (/docs directory)
   - Blog Content (/blog directory)
   - Static Assets (/static directory)
   - Custom Components (/src/components)

d. Deployment Layer:
   - GitHub Actions CI/CD (from .github/workflows)
   - GitHub Pages Hosting

2. Component Relationships:

Draw the diagram with these flows:
```
[Content Files] → [Build System] → [Static Output] → [Deployment]
                     ↑
            [Development Server]
                     ↑
         [Development Environment]
```

3. Specific Implementation Details:

Use different shapes/colors to represent:
- Rectangle boxes for main components
- Hexagons for build tools
- Cylinders for content stores
- Arrows showing build and deployment flow
- Dotted lines for development-time connections

4. Important Elements to Highlight:

a. Content Organization:
   - Show the hierarchical structure of docs/features, docs/tutorials, etc.
   - Highlight the separation between documentation and blog content

b. Build Process:
   - Show how Docusaurus processes MDX/MD files
   - Indicate the role of CSS processing (Tailwind/PostCSS)
   - Show TypeScript compilation process (noted from tsconfig.json)

c. Deployment Flow:
   - Illustrate GitHub Actions workflow
   - Show the gh-pages deployment process

5. Additional Considerations:

- Include a section showing the local development feedback loop
- Highlight the static nature of the final output
- Show integration points with external services (if any)
- Include configuration management (environment variables, etc.)

6. Legend:

Create a legend that explains:
- Color coding (e.g., blue for content, green for build tools)
- Arrow types (solid for build flow, dotted for development flow)
- Shape meanings (rectangles, hexagons, cylinders)
- Component groupings

7. Level of Detail:

Keep the main diagram at a high level showing the primary components and flows, but consider creating sub-diagrams for:
- Content organization structure
- Build process details
- Deployment pipeline

The diagram should emphasize the static site generation nature of the project while showing how the development and deployment processes work together to create and serve the documentation website.

Remember to include annotations explaining key architectural decisions and any specific Docusaurus-related configurations that affect the system's behavior.

This documentation site appears to be comprehensive, so consider creating a separate view showing how the content organization maps to the final URL structure, as this is crucial for documentation systems.
